correctness.description: The host's own suite, tests/test_predictor.cpp: an always-taken branch is learned, a never-taken branch is learned, and two PCs in different bimodal entries do not train each other. The port adds a second test file rather than editing this one.
G2 on the smoke workload: with the knob off, both metrics must equal the recorded baseline exactly. The host is deterministic, so this is an equality, not a comparison within noise.

The same equality on the workload the performance entry uses. Worth its own entry: the feature is designed to move this one, so a knob-off leak would show up here first and would otherwise be indistinguishable from the gain.

With TINYSC_ENABLE unset, every prediction over a driven stream equals the unmodified base predictor's for the same stream. The case sets its own environment before constructing anything, because params.h reads the environment on every call; on failure it must print exactly 'FAIL: disabled path matches the base predictor'.

pass_condition.pattern: ok: disabled path matches the base predictor

correctness.description: With TINYSC_ENABLE=1, one PC following the period-4 pattern taken, taken, not-taken, not-taken for 400 branches must mispredict at most 5 times over the last 100, where the base predictor alone misses about half. This is the case that distinguishes a corrector wired to global history from one that is not. On success it must print exactly 'ok: history-correlated branch is learned'.

With TINYSC_ENABLE=1, a PC seen for the first time selects a counter still at zero, which is not confident at any threshold of 1 or more, so the base prediction must stand. On success it must print exactly 'ok: untrained entry defers to the base predictor'.

pass_condition.pattern: ok: untrained entry defers to the base predictor

performance.description: The claimed benefit on the workload built to need it. bias.trace emits five PCs round-robin: two are history-correlated and account for most of the baseline's 2818 mispredictions out of 6000 branches, two are strongly biased and already predicted well, and one is random and helps nobody. A port that builds, stays baseline-identical with its knob off, and still does not move MPKI here has a mechanism that is wired wrong.

warn_threshold.claim_source: Derived, not quoted: the fixture spec makes no whole-workload claim. /unit_tests/1 claims at most 5 mispredictions per 100 on a history-correlated branch where the base predictor misses about half, and the two history-correlated PCs are two fifths of bias.trace and roughly 1800 of its 2818 baseline mispredictions, so recovering most of them is about a 0.5 relative reduction.

notes: min_relative_improvement is 0.0 and max_relative_regression is 0.0 because this host is exactly reproducible: src/sim.cpp charges a fixed instruction count per branch and a fixed misprediction penalty, so there is no noise band to leave room for, and IPC is a strictly decreasing function of mispredictions. A real host sets both above its measured run-to-run spread.
